metadata.title: Heat kernel for non-local operators with variable order

extraction_notes.note: Remark 1.5 has a sketched proof for its item (1) only; item (1) is emitted as a claim nested in the remark and the sketch proves that claim, while the remark's \ref to the sketch is kept as a mention.

Remark 2.2 states an integral estimate obtained from the proof of Chen-Zhang Lemma 2.1(i) and is used repeatedly; kept as an external remark rather than an external lemma because the environment is a remark and part of its text is commentary.
The Levi-method ansatz (p = p^y + correction, q solving an integral equation with kernel q_0) is typed as a definition of q_0, q and p rather than as an algorithm.

The lower bounds of Theorem 1.1 are proved in Corollary 5.10 via Propositions 5.6-5.9, whose proofs use the Chapman-Kolmogorov equation and generator identities (1.11), (1.15) that are proved in step (v) of the main proof; the argument is not circular, but at node granularity this gives a cycle through Theorem 1.1, kept as is.

The label t5-1-2 is used twice (Theorem 1.3 and Proposition 4.7); the parser resolves it to Theorem 1.3, so the \\eqref in the proof of Proposition 4.7 is kept only as a mention edge. References to the definition of rho (e3-0) and to equation (1.1) inside Theorem 1.1 are likewise marked as mentions.
The parser's structure for the proof of Proposition 2.9 misses the label Case (e) and the Subcases (c1)/(c2) in the proof of Lemma 3.1; steps were added for them by hand.
Corollary 5.10 has no proof environment; its justification is the lead-in sentence 'According to Propositions ... we immediately get the following', which has no closing punctuation.

Literature results mentioned in the Background (Bass, Chen-Kumagai, Chen-Zhang, Kolokoltsov) are only cited, not stated, and got no nodes; unnumbered displays and notational conventions inside proofs stay in their containing nodes.

metadata.extraction_comment: Most labelled proof steps follow the paper's (i)/(1)/Case labels only; long label bodies (some several pages) were not subdivided further.

nodes.statement: (1) We first suppose that kappa(x,z) is independent of z. Case (a): |x-y|leqslant t^1/alpha(y). According to , we can choose 0<gamma<beta_0/alpha_2 and adjust the constants properly to get that |q_0(t,x-y)|&preceq rho^y,beta_0_-gamma(t,x-y)preceq t^-gamma|x-y|^beta_0cdotrho^y,0_0(t,x-y)\\ &preceq t^(beta_0/alpha_2)-gammarho^y,0_0(t,x-y)preceq rho^y,0_0(t,x-y)preceq t^-(d/alpha(y))-1, where in the third inequality we have used the fact that |x-y|leqslant t^1/alpha(y)leqslant t^1/alpha_2, and the fourth inequality follows from gamma<beta_0/alpha_2. Case (b): |x-y|>t^1/alpha(y). By , it holds that | mathcal L^x p^y(t,cdot)(x-y)|& preceq int_\|z|leqslant |x-y|/2\left| delta_p^yleft(t,x-y;zright)right|frac1|z|^d+alpha(x)\,dz\\ & +int_\|z|> |x-y|/2\left| delta_p^yleft(t,x-y;zright)right|frac1|z|^d+alpha(x)\,dz\\ &=:J_1+J_2. Then, using the mean value theorem, we have J_1&preceq int_\|z|leqslant |x-y|/2\ left|nabla^2 p^y(t,x-y+theta_x,y,z z)right|cdot |z|^2frac1|z|^d+alpha(x)\,dz\\ &preceq int_\|z|leqslant |x-y|/2\ fractleft(t^1/alpha(y)+|x-y+theta_x,y,z z|right)^d+alpha(y)+2 cdot |z|^2-d-alpha(x)\,dz\\ &preceq fractleft(t^1/alpha(y)+|x-y|right)^d+alpha(y)+2 int_\|z|leqslant |x-y|/2\ |z|^2-d-alpha(x)\,dz\\ &preceq frac|x-y|^alpha(y)|x-y|^d+alpha(y)+2cdot |x-y|^2-alpha(x)preceq frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(x), where in the first inequality theta_x,y,z is a constant depending on x,y,z such that |theta_x,y,z|leqslant 1, in the second inequality we have used , the third inequality follows from the fact that |x-y+theta_x,y,z z|geqslant |x-y|-|z|geqslant |x-y|/2, and the fourth inequality is due to the fact that tleqslant |x-y|^alpha(y). On the other hand, by and the fact that |z|>|x-y|/2geqslant t^1/alpha(y)/2, we have left|delta_p^y(t,x-y;z)right|preceq rho^y,0_1(t,x-ypm z)+rho^y,0_1(t,x-y), and so J_2&preceq int_\|z|>|x-y|/2\\!\! rho^y,0_1(t,x-ypm z)frac1|z|^d+alpha(x)\,dz + rho^y,0_1(t,x-y)int_\|z|>|x-y|/2\\!\! frac1|z|^d+alpha(x)\,dz=:J_21+J_22. It holds that J_21&preceq frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(x) int_\|z|>|x-y|/2\rho^y,0_1(t,x-ypm z)\,dzpreceq frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(x)int rho^y,0_1(t,x-ypm z)\,dzpreceq frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(x), where in the first inequality we have used following fact frac1|z|^d+alpha(x)preceq frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(x) for |z|>|x-y|/2, and the last inequality follows from . Furthermore, it is easy to verify that J_22&preceq rho^y,0_1(t,x-y) int_\|z|>|x-y|/2\frac1|z|^d+alpha(x)\, dzpreceq fract|x-y|^d+alpha(x)+alpha(y)preceq frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(x), where in the last inequality we used |x-y|leqslant t^1/alpha(y). Combining all these estimates above, we arrive at left| mathcal L^xp^y(t,cdot)(x-y)right|preceq frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(x). Following the same arguments as above, we also have left| mathcal L^yp^y(t,cdot)(x-y)right|preceq frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(y). Hence, |q_0(t,x,y)|&preceq left| mathcal L^x p^y(t,cdot)(x-y)right|+left| mathcal L^yp^y(t,cdot)(x-y)right|preceq frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(x)+frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(y), from which we can get immediately. (2) Next we consider the case that kappa(x,z) depends on z. With the estimate and the condition beta_0/alpha_2>(alpha_2/alpha_1)-1 at hand, we can follow the same argument as in to verify the upper bound in for the case that |x-y|leqslant t^1/alpha(y). When |x-y|>t^1/alpha(y), we still define J_1 and J_2 via . By carefully tracking the proof above, we find that the argument for the estimates of J_2 in part (1) still works. So it remains to consider upper bound for J_1. According to , we have J_1&preceq int_\|z|leqslant |x-y|/2\ big[big(t^-2/alpha(y)|z|^2big)wedge 1big] cdot big(rho_1^y,0(t,x-ypm z)+rho_1^y,0(t,x-y)big)frac1|z|^d+alpha(x)\,dz\\ &preceq fract|x-y|^d+alpha(y)int big[big(t^-2/alpha(y)|z|^2big)wedge 1big] cdot frac1|z|^d+alpha(x)\,dz\\ &preceq fract|x-y|^d+alpha(y)cdot bigg(int_\|z|leqslant t^1/alpha(y)\ t^-2/alpha(y)|z|^2-d-alpha(x)\,dz+int_\|z|> t^1/alpha(y)\|z|^-d-alpha(x)\,dzbigg)\\ &preceq t^1-(alpha(x)/alpha(y))cdot frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(y)preceq t^1-(alpha_2/alpha_1)cdot frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(y), where the second inequality above follows from rho^y,0_1(t,x-ypm z)preceq fract|x-y|^d+alpha(y) for any |z|leqslant |x-y|/2. Combining this with the estimate of J_2 in part (1) yields |q_0(t,x,y)|&preceq left| mathcal L^x p^y(t,cdot)(x-y)right|+left| mathcal L^xp^y(t,cdot)(x-y)right|preceq t^1-(alpha_2/alpha_1)cdot bigg(frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(x)+frac1|x-y|^d+alpha(y)bigg), which implies that holds for every x,y in mathds R^d with |x-y|>t^1/alpha(y). The proof is complete.

nodes.statement: item[(1)] If kappa(x,z)=kappa (x) is independent of z, then for any gamma,theta>0 with gamma<theta<beta_0/alpha_2 and any varepsilon>0, there exists a positive constant c_1:=c_1(alpha,kappa, gamma, theta,varepsilon) such that for every (t,x,x',y)in (0,1]times mathds R^dtimes mathds R^d times mathds R^d, &|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\ &leqslant c_1left(|x-x'|^alpha_1(beta_0-alpha_2theta)/alpha(x)wedge 1right)\\ & timesBig[left(rho^y,0_theta-gamma+rho^y,beta_0_theta-gamma-(beta_0/alpha(x))right)(t,x-y) +left(rho^y,0_theta-gamma+rho^y,beta_0_theta-gamma-(beta_0/alpha(x'))right)(t,x'-y)\\ & +|x-y|^varepsilonmathds 1_\|x-y|>R_0\rho^y,0_theta-gamma(t,x-y) +|x'-y|^varepsilonmathds 1_\|x'-y|>R_0\rho^y,0_theta-gamma(t,x'-y)Big]. item[(2)] For general kappa (x, z), if (alpha_2/alpha_1)-1<beta_0/alpha_2, then for any gamma,theta>0 such that (alpha_2/alpha_1)-1+gamma =:gamma_2 <theta<beta_0/alpha_2 and varepsilon>0, there exists a positive constant c_2:=c_2(alpha,kappa,gamma,theta,varepsilon) such that for every (t,x,x',y)in (0,1]times mathds R^dtimes mathds R^d times mathds R^d, & |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\ &leqslant c_2left(|x-x'|^alpha_1(beta_0-alpha_2theta)/alpha(x)wedge 1right) Big[left(rho^y,0_theta-gamma_2 +rho^y,beta_0_theta-gamma_2-(beta_0/alpha(x))right)(t,x-y)\\ & +left(rho^y,0_theta-gamma_2+rho^y,beta_0_theta-gamma_2 -(beta_0/alpha(x'))right)(t,x'-y) +|x-y|^varepsilonmathds 1_\|x-y|>R_0\rho^y,0_theta-gamma_2 (t,x-y)\\ & +|x'-y|^varepsilonmathds 1_\|x'-y|>R_0\rho^y,0_theta-gamma_2 (t,x'-y)Big].

nodes.statement: In the remainder of this paper, we denote nabla p^y(t,cdot)(x) by nabla p^y(t,x) for simplicity. (1) We first consider the case that kappa(x,z) is independent of z. Let R_1:=R_1(alpha,kappa,gamma) be a positive constant to be determined later. The proof is split into the following five different cases. Case (a): |x-x'|>R_1. By and the condition beta_0>alpha_2theta, it holds that |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)| &leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)|+|q_0(t,x',y)|preceq rho_-gamma^y,beta_0(t,x-y)+rho_-gamma^y,beta_0(t,x'-y)\\ &preceq big(|x-x'|^alpha_1(beta_0-alpha_2theta)/alpha(x)wedge1big)big(rho_-gamma^y,beta_0(t,x-y)+rho_-gamma^y,beta_0(t,x'-y)big). Case (b): C_0t^1/alpha(y)leqslant |x-x'|leqslant R_1 for some small constant C_0>0. According to again, we have |q_0(t,x,y)|preceq& rho_-gamma^y,beta_0(t,x-y)preceq t^(beta_0-alpha(x)theta)/alpha(x) rho_-gamma+theta-(beta_0/alpha(x))^y,beta_0(t,x-y) \\ preceq&|x-x'|^alpha(y)(beta_0-alpha(x)theta)/alpha(x) rho_-gamma+theta-(beta_0/alpha(x))^y,beta_0(t,x-y) \\ preceq&|x-x'|^alpha_1(beta_0-alpha_2theta)/alpha(x) rho_-gamma+theta-(beta_0/alpha(x))^y,beta_0(t,x-y), where the third inequality is due to tpreceq |x-x'|^alpha(y). Then &|q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|\\ &leqslant |q_0(t,x,y)|+|q_0(t,x',y)|\\ &preceq |x-\!x'|^alpha_1(beta_0-alpha_2theta)/alpha(x) \! rho_-gamma+theta-(beta_0/alpha(x))^y,beta_0(t,x-y) + |x-\!x'|^alpha_1(beta_0-alpha_2theta)/alpha(x')\! rho_-gamma+theta-(beta_0/alpha(x'))^y,beta_0(t,x'\!-y)\\ &preceq |x-\!x'|^alpha_1(beta_0-alpha_2theta)/alpha(x)Big( rho_-gamma+theta-(beta_0/alpha(x))^y,beta_0(t,x\!-y)+ rho_-gamma+theta-(beta_0/alpha(x'))^y,beta_0(t,x'\!-y)Big). Here in the last inequality we have used the fact that for x,x'in mathds R^d with |x-x'|leqslant R_1, |x-x'|^alpha_1(beta_0-alpha_2theta)/alpha(x')preceq |x-x'|^alpha_1(beta_0-alpha_2theta)/alpha(x), which can be verified by following the argument of . Next, we mainly treat the case that |x-x'|leqslant C_0t^1/alpha(y), which we divide into three cases. Case (c): |x-x'|leqslant C_0t^1/alpha(y) and |x-y|geqslant R_1. By the definition of q_0(t,x,y), |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)| &=frac12bigg|int_mathds R^d delta_p^y(t,x-y;z)bigg(frackappa(x,z)|z|^d+alpha(x)-frackappa(y,z)|z|^d+alpha(y) bigg)\,dz\\ & -int_mathds R^d delta_p^y(t,x'-y;z)bigg(frackappa(x',z)|z|^d+alpha(x')-frackappa(y,z)|z|^d+alpha(y) bigg)\,dzbigg|\\ &leqslant frac12int_mathds R^d |delta_p^y(t,x-y;z)-delta_p^y(t,x'-y;z)| bigg|frackappa(x,z)|z|^d+alpha(x)-frackappa(y,z)|z|^d+alpha(y) bigg|\,dz\\ & + frac12int_mathds R^d |delta_p^y(t,x'-y;z)| bigg|frackappa(x',z)|z|^d+alpha(x')-frackappa(x,z)|z|^d+alpha(x) bigg|\,dz\\ &=:J_1+J_2. Note that delta_p^y(t,x;z)=&p^y(t,x+z)+p^y(t,x-z)-2p^y(t,x)\\ =&int_0^1 fracddthetaBig(p^y(t,x+theta z)+p^y(t,x-theta z)Big)\,dtheta\\ =&int_0^1 langle nabla p^y(t,x+theta z)-nabla p^y(t,x-theta z),zrangle \,dtheta\\ =&int_0^1 Biglangle int_-1^1 fracdd theta'left(nabla p^y(t,x+theta'theta z)right)dtheta',z Bigrangle \,dtheta\\ =&int_0^1int_-1^1 nabla^2 p^y(t,x+theta'theta z)(theta z, z)dtheta'\,dtheta, and so delta_p^y(t,x;z)-delta_p^y(t,x';z) &=int_0^1int_-1^1 big(nabla^2 p^y(t,x+theta'theta z)- nabla^2 p^y(t,x'+theta'theta z)big)(theta z, z)\,dtheta'\,dtheta\\ &=int_0^1int_-1^1int_0^1 fracddtheta''Big(nabla^2 p^y(t,x'+theta''(x-x')+theta'theta z)Big) (theta z, z)\,dtheta''dtheta'\,dtheta\\ &=int_0^1int_-1^1int_0^1 nabla^3 p^y(t,x'+theta''(x-x')+theta'theta z) (x-x',theta z, z)\,dtheta''dtheta'\,dtheta, which implies that |delta_p^y(t,x;z)-delta_p^y(t,x';z) | &leqslant Big(int_0^1int_-1^1int_0^1 |nabla^3 p^y(t,x'+theta''(x-x')+theta'theta z)|\,\,dtheta''dtheta'\,dthetaBig) cdot |z|^2|x-x'|. For every x,x',zinmathds R^d with |x-x'|leqslant C_0 t^1/alpha(y), |x|geqslant cR_1, |x'|geqslant cR_1 and |z|leqslant cR_1/4 for C_0 small enough, there exists a constant c'>0 such that for every thetain(0,1), theta'in(-1,1) and theta''in(0,1), we have |x'+theta''(x-x')+theta'theta z|geqslant c'|x'|geqslant c''R_1, which along with yields that |nabla^3 p^y(t,x'+theta''(x-x')+theta'theta z)| preceq fract|x'|^d+alpha(y)+3. Combining with all the estimates above, we arrive at that for |x-x'|leqslant C_0t^1/alpha(y), |x|geqslant cR_1, |x'|geqslant cR_1 and |z|leqslant cR_1/4, |delta_p^y(t,x;z)-delta_p^y(t,x';z) |preceq fract|z|^2|x-x'||x'|^d+alpha(y)+3. Since |x-x'|leqslant C_0t^1/alpha(y)leqslant C_0, |x'-y|geqslant cR_1 holds for some constant c>0. By taking x=x-y and x'=x'-y in , we obtain that for all zinmathds R^d with |z|leqslant cR_1/4, |delta_p^y(t,x-y;z)-delta_p^y(t,x'-y;z) |preceq fract|z|^2|x-x'||x'-y|^d+alpha(y)+3. Let J_1=&frac12int_\|z|leqslant cR_1/4\ |delta_p^y(t,x-y;z)-delta_p^y(t,x'-y;z)| bigg|frackappa(x,z)|z|^d+alpha(x)-frackappa(y,z)|z|^d+alpha(y) bigg|\,dz\\ &+ frac12int_\|z|> cR_1/4\ |delta_p^y(t,x-y;z)-delta_p^y(t,x'-y;z)| bigg|frackappa(x,z)|z|^d+alpha(x)-frackappa(y,z)|z|^d+alpha(y) bigg|\,dz\\ =&:J_11+J_12. By , J_11preceq &|x-x'|fract|x'-y|^d+alpha(y)+3 int_\|z|leqslant cR_1/4\bigg( frac|z|^2|z|^d+alpha(x)+frac|z|^2|z|^d+alpha(y) bigg)\,dz\\ preceq& |x-x'|fract|x'-y|^d+alpha(y)+3 preceq |x-x'|frac1|x'-y|^d+alpha_1, where the last inequality is due to |x'-y|>cR_1 and tleqslant 1. On the other hand, according to , we have for any x,yinmathds R^d with |x-y|>R_1, &int_\|z|>cR_1/4\ rho_1^y,0(t,x-ypm z) frac1|z|^d+alpha (x)\,dz preceq frac1|x-y|^d+alpha_1,\\ &int_\|z|>cR_1/4\ rho_1^y,0(t,x-y) frac1|z|^d+alpha (x)\,dz preceq frac1|x-y|^d+alpha_1. Combining with and the fact that |z|>cR_1/4 implies |z|>C_1t^1/alpha(y), we arrive at J_12&preceq t^-1/alpha(y)|x-x'| int_\|z|>cR_1/4\Big(rho_1^y,0(t,x-ypm z)+rho_1^y,0(t,x-y)\\ & +rho_1^y,0(t,x'-ypm z)+rho_1^y,0(t,x'-y)Big) bigg(frac1|z|^d+alpha(x)+frac1|z|^d+alpha(y) bigg)\,dz\\ &preceq t^-1/alpha(y)|x-x'| left( frac1|x-y|^d+alpha_1+ frac1|x'-y|^d+alpha_1 right). By both of the estimates above, we obtain that J_1&preceq t^-1/alpha(y)|x-x'| big( rho_0^y,0(t,x-y)+rho_0^y,0(t,x'-y)big)preceq |x-x'| big( rho_-1/alpha(y)^y,beta_0(t,x-y)+rho_-1/alpha(y)^y,beta_0(t,x'-y)big), where the last inequality follows from the facts that |x-y|geqslant cR_1 and |x'-y|geqslant c R_1. Let J_2=&int_\|z|leqslant cR_1/4\ |delta_p^y(t,x'-y;z)| bigg|frackappa(x',z)|z|^d+alpha(x')-frackappa(x,z)|z|^d+alpha(x) bigg|\,dz\\ &+ int_\|z|> cR_1/4\ |delta_p^y(t,x'-y;z)| bigg|frackappa(x',z)|z|^d+alpha(x')-frackappa(x,z)|z|^d+alpha(x) bigg|\,dz\\ =&:J_21+J_22. Since |x'-y|>cR_1, by and , we find that for any |z|<cR_1/4 , |delta_p^y(t,x'-y;z)|&leqslant |z|^2int_0^1int_-1^1 |nabla^2 p^y(t,x'-y+theta'theta z)|\,dtheta'\,dtheta preceq |z|^2 frac t |x'-y|^d+alpha(y)+2. Thus, due to , J_21 preceq& |x-x'|^beta_0 fract|x'-y|^d+alpha(y)+2int_\|z|leqslant cR_1/4\ \!\!frac1+|log |z|||z|^d+overlinealpha(x;x')|z|^2\,dz preceq |x-x'|^beta_0 frac1|x'-y|^d+alpha_1, where we have used the facts that |x'-y|>cR_1 and t<1 in the second inequality. On the other hand, when |z|> cR_1/4, |delta_p^y(t,x'-y;z)|preceq p^y(t,x'-ypm z)+p^y(t,x'-y). Having this at hand and using and , we know that int_\|z|>cR_1/4\ |delta_p^y(t,x'-y;z)|frac1+|log|z|||z|^d+underlinealpha(x;x')\,dz preceq fraclog(1+|x'-y|)|x'-y|^d+alpha_1. Then, by , we find that J_22&preceq |x-x'|^beta_0cdot int_\|z|>cR_1/4\|delta_p^y(t,x'-y;z)|frac1+|log|z|||z|^d+underlinealpha(x;x')\,dz preceq |x-x'|^beta_0fraclog(1+|x'-y|)|x'-y|^d+alpha_1. By the estimates for J_21 and J_22, we have J_2preceq |x-x'|^beta_0log(1+|x'-y|)rho^y,0_0(t,x'-y). Putting the estimates of J_1 and J_2 together, we finally arrive at |q_0(t,x,y)-q_0(t,x',y)|preceq & |x-x'|big( rho_-1/alpha(y)^y,beta_0(t,x-y)+rho_-1/alpha(y)^y,beta_0(t,x'-y)big)\\ &+|x-x'|^beta_0log(1+|x'-y|)rho^y,0_0(t,x'-y). Case (d): |x-x'|leqslant C_0t^1/alpha(y) and t^1/alpha(y)leqslant |x-y|< R_1. We still define J_1 and J_2 by those in . Combining with , we arrive at J_1 preceq & t^-1/alpha(y)|x-x'||x-y|^beta_0Bigg[int_mathds R^d left[left(t^-2/alpha(y)|z|^2right)wedge 1right]\\ & times big( rho_1^y,0(t,x-y)+rho_1^y,0(t,x'-y)+rho_1^y,0(t,x-ypm z)+rho_1^y,0(t,x'-ypm z)big)\\ & timesbigg(frac1+|log|z|||z|^d+overlinealpha(y;x)mathds 1_\|z|leqslant 1\+frac1+|log|z|||z|^d+underlinealpha(y;x)mathds 1_\|z|> 1\bigg)\,dzBigg]. Noting that t^1/alpha(y)leqslant |x-y|< R_1 and using --, we obtain that & int_mathds R^d left[left(t^-2/alpha(y)|z|^2right)wedge 1right]big (rho_1^y,0(t,x-ypm z)+rho_1^y,0(t,x-y)big)\\ & times bigg(frac1+|log|z|||z|^d+overlinealpha(y;x)mathds 1_\|z|leqslant 1\ +frac1+|log|z|||z|^d+underlinealpha(y;x)mathds 1_\|z|> 1\bigg)\,dz\\ &preceq left(1+|log t|right)t^-(overlinealpha(y;x)-alpha(y))/alpha(y) rho_0^y,0(t,x-y)preceq rho_-gamma^y,0(t,x-y), where the last step is due to the fact that we can choose the constant R_1 small enough such that fracoverlinealpha(y;x)-alpha(y)alpha(y)leqslant fracC|x-y|^beta_0alpha_1<gamma for every |x-y|leqslant R_1. Since |x-x'|leqslant C_0 t^1/alpha(y) for some C_0 small enough, C_2t^1/alpha(y)leqslant |x'-y|leqslant C_3R_1 holds for some positive constants C_2 and C_3. Hence, still holds with x replaced by x'. Therefore, combining both the estimates above together, we arrive at J_1 &preceq |x-x'|cdot |x-y|^beta_0cdot left(rho^y,0_-gamma-(1/alpha(y))(t,x-y)+rho^y,0_-gamma-(1/alpha(y))(t,x'-y)right)\\ &preceq |x-x'|left(rho^y,beta_0_-gamma-(1/alpha(y))(t,x-y)+rho^y,beta_0_-gamma-(1/alpha(y))(t,x'-y)right), where in the last step we have used the fact that |x'-y|geqslant |x-y|-|x-x'| geqslant |x-y|-C_0t^1/alpha(y)geqslant (1-C_0)|x-y|. Now we are going to estimate J_2. along with yields that J_2 & preceq |x-x'|^beta_0int_mathds R^dleft[left(t^-2/alpha(y)|z|^2right)wedge 1right]cdotBig( rho_1^y,0(t,x'\!-y)\!+rho_1^y,0(t,x'\!-ypm z)Big)\\ & times bigg(frac|log|z||+1|z|^d+overlinealpha(x;x')mathds 1_\|z|leqslant 1\ \!+frac|log|z||+1|z|^d+underlinealpha(x;x')mathds 1_\|z|> 1\\!\!bigg)\,dz. the upper bound given in \cite[Therem 1.1]{CZ}.

where $\kappa_1>0$ is the constant in \eqref{e1-2}, $\widehat \kappa(y,z):=\kappa(y,z)-\kappa_1/2$ and
$$\delta_f(x;z)=f(x+z)+f(x-z)-2f(x).$$ Then, we have
\begin{equation}\label{l4-4-2}
p^y(t,x)=\int_{\mathds R^d}p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x-z)p^y_{\widehat \kappa}(t,z)\,dz,\ \ x\in \mathds R^d, t\in (0,1],
\end{equation}
where $p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}$ and $p^y_{\widehat \kappa}$ denote the fundamental solutions (i.e.\ heat kernel) associated with
the operators ${\mathcal L}_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}^y$ and ${\mathcal L}_{\widehat \kappa}^y$, respectively.

We first show that \eqref{l4-4-1} holds for $p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}$. Indeed, for every $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ such that $|x-x'|\leqslant 1$,
\begin{align*}

\left|\int_0^1 \frac{d}{d \theta}\left(\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}
\left(1,x+\theta(x'-x)\right)\right)\,d\theta\right|\\
&\leqslant |x-x'|\cdot\int_0^1 \left|\nabla^2 p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}
\left(1,x+\theta(x'-x)\right)\right|\,d\theta\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \int_0^1 \left(1+\left|x+\theta(x'-x)\right|\right)^{-d-\alpha(y)-2}\,d\theta\\
&\preceq |x-x'|\cdot \left(1+|x|\right)^{-d-\alpha(y)-2},
\end{align*}
where in the third inequality we have used \eqref{p1-1-1}, and the last inequality is due to
the fact that for all $\theta\in [0,1]$ and $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|\leqslant 1$
\begin{equation*}
\left(1+\left|x+\theta(x'-x)\right|\right)^{-1}\preceq \left(1+|x|\right)^{-1}.
\end{equation*}
Also by \eqref{p1-1-1}, we have that for every
$x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-x'|>1$,
\begin{align*}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|&
\leqslant \big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)\big|+
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|\\
&\preceq (1+|x|)^{-d-\alpha(y)-1}+
(1+|x'|)^{-d-\alpha(y)-1}.
\end{align*}
Combining both estimates above yields that for all $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$,
\begin{equation}\label{l4-4-3}
\begin{split}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,x')\big|
\preceq &\left(|x-x'|\wedge 1\right)\left(
(1+|x|)^{-d-\alpha(y)}+
(1+|x'|)^{-d-\alpha(y)}\right).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Since the Markov process $(X_t^{y,{\kappa_1}/{2}})_{t\geqslant0}$ associated with
$ {\mathcal L}^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}$ is a constant time-change of standard rotationally invariant $\alpha(y)$-stable process, by
the scaling property, for all $t>0$ and $x \in \mathds R^d$,
$$
 p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x)= t^{-d/\alpha(y)} p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(1,t^{-1/\alpha(y)}x).
$$
This along with \eqref{l4-4-3} yields that for all $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$,
\begin{equation}\label{l4-4-4}
\begin{split}
\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x')\big|
\preceq &\left[\left(t^{-1/\alpha(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\left(
\rho_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}^{y,0}(t,x)+\rho_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}^{y,0}(t,x')\right).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Therefore,  for every $x,x'\in \mathds R^d$ and $t\in (0,1]$,
\begin{align*}
&\left|\nabla p^y(t,x)-\nabla p^y(t,x')\right|\\
&=\left|\int_{\mathds R^d}\big(\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x-z)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x'-z)\big)
\cdot p^y_{\widehat \kappa}(t,z)\,dz\right|\\
&\leqslant \int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x-z)-\nabla p^y_{{\kappa_1}/{2}}(t,x'-z)\big|
\cdot p^y_{\widehat \kappa}(t,z)\,dz\\
&\preceq \left[\left(t^{-1/\alpha(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\cdot
\Bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x-z)\rho^{y,0}_1(t,z)\,dz+\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x'-z)\rho^{y,0}_1(t,z)\,dz\Bigg)\\
&\preceq  \left[\left(t^{-1/\alpha(y)}|x-x'|\right)\wedge 1\right]\cdot
\left(\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x)
+\rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(y))}(t,x')\right),
\end{align*}
where the equality above is due to \eqref{l4-4-2}, the second inequality follows from
\eqref{l4-4-4} and \eqref{p1-1-1-1-0}, and in the last inequality we have used
\eqref{l3-2-1-}. By now we have finished the proof.

we find by \eqref{t5-1-3} that for every (small enough) $\gamma>0$, there is a constant $R_1:=R_1(\alpha, \kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{t5-1-4}\begin{split}
|\nabla p^z(t,x-z)|&\preceq
\begin{cases}
\rho^{z,0}_{1-({1}/{\alpha(z)})}(t,x-z),\ &|x-z|\leqslant R_1,\\
\frac{t}{|x-z|^{d+\alpha_1+1}}
,\ & |x-z|>R_1
\end{cases}\\
&\preceq \rho^{z,0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x)})-\gamma}(t,x-z). \end{split}
\end{equation}

\eqref{t5-1-4}, we can find that
\begin{align*}
&\int_0^{t/2}\int_{\mathds R^d}|J_1(s,z)|\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq
\int_0^{t/2}\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)
\big(
\rho^{y,0}_{({\beta_0}/{\alpha_2})-\gamma}(s,z-y)+
\rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma}(s,z-y)\big)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \rho^{y,0}_0(t,x_0-y)\!\bigg(\!\int_0^{t/2}\!(t\!-\!s)^{-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-\gamma}\! +\!

On the other hand, according to \eqref{p3-1-1a}, \eqref{t5-1-4} and the fact that $\beta_0<\alpha(x_0)$, we arrive at
\begin{align*}

&\preceq \int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}
\bigg(\rho^{z,\widehat \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\tilde\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}
(s,z-y)
\\

+\rho^{z,\widehat \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\tilde\rho^{y,0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(s,x_0-y)\bigg)\,dz\,ds\\
&=:\int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}(J_{21}(s,z)+J_{22}(s,z))\,dz\,ds,
\end{align*}
where $\widehat \beta_0=\widehat \beta_0(\theta):={\alpha_1(\beta_0-\alpha_2\theta)}/{\alpha(x_0)}$.

Since $\tilde \beta_0(x_0)>1-\alpha(x_0)$, we can choose
$\theta, \gamma>0$ small enough such that $1+(\widehat \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma>0$, which along with
\eqref{l3-2-0} yields
\begin{align*}

\int_{t/2}^t (t-s)^{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{-1+\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}\\

(1/\alpha(x_0))-\gamma}s^{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}\,ds\Big)\\
&\preceq\tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1-(1/\alpha(x_0))+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)-2\gamma}(t,x_0-y).
\end{align*}
On the other hand, noting that for $t/2<s\leqslant t$, it holds that
\begin{equation}\label{t5-1-5}
\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{\theta-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(s,x_0-y)\preceq
\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-{(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}}(t,x_0-y).
\end{equation}
Since $\tilde \beta_0>1-\alpha(x_0)$, by \eqref{l3-1-1} we have
\begin{align*}
 \int_{t/2}^t \int_{\mathds R^d}J_{22}(s,z)\,dz\,ds
&\preceq
\tilde \rho^{y,\beta_0}_{-\gamma+(\beta_0/\alpha_2)-(\beta_0/\alpha_1)}(t,x_0-y)
\int_{t/2}^t\int_{\mathds R^d}\rho^{z,\widehat \beta_0}_{1-({1/\alpha(x_0)})-\gamma}(t-s,x_0-z)\,dz\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{y,0}_{1+(\widehat \beta_0/\alpha(x_0))-(1/\alpha(x_0))+

\tilde \rho^{z,\beta_0}_{1-1/\alpha(x_0)-\gamma}(t,x_0-z).
\end{align*}

$$

\eqref{t5-1-2} holds.

&\quad+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\!\!\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)
\big(\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big)\,dw\bigg)\,ds.
\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{align*}
& \int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(t,x-y;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t,x-y;z)\big|\cdot\frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\\
& \leqslant \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^x(s,w)\big|
\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\
&+\int_{{t}/{2}}^t\bigg[\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big|
\bigg(\int_{\mathds R^d}\big|\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|\cdot \frac{1}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg)\,dw\bigg]\,ds\\
&=:J_1+J_2.
\end{align*}


According to \eqref{p1-1-4} and \eqref{l4-1-5}, for every $\theta \in (0,1)$ and $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant
$R_1:=R_1(\alpha,\kappa,\gamma)>0$ such that for every $0<s<t<1$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation}\label{l4-2-2}
\begin{split}
&\big|\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y-w;z)-\delta_{p^y}(t-s,x-y;z)\big|\\
&\preceq \big[\left((t-s)^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}|w|\right)^{\theta}\wedge 1\big]\cdot
\left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(y)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\\
&\quad\times\big[
\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w)
+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_1^{y,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big]\\
&\preceq \left(|w|^{\theta}\wedge 1\right)\cdot
\left[\left((t-s)^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
 \cdot\big[
\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w)\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad\quad
+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y\pm z)+\rho_{1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}^{x,0}(t-s,x-y-w\pm z)\big].
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Furthermore, following the argument of Lemma \ref{l1-1}, we can derive that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$
\begin{equation}\label{l4-2-3}
\begin{split}
&\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y \pm z)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz
\preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y),\\
&\int_{\mathds R^d} \left[\left(t^{-{2}/{\alpha(x)}}|z|^2\right)\wedge 1\right]
\cdot \rho_{1}^{x,0}(t,y)\cdot |z|^{-d-\alpha(x)}\,dz
\preceq \rho^{x,0}_{0}(t,y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{l4-1-4} with \eqref{l4-2-2} and \eqref{l4-2-3}, we find that for  all $t\in(0,1]$ and  $x,y\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{align*}
J_1 &\preceq |x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot \bigg[
\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\cdot
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y-w)\,dw\,ds\\
&\qquad\qquad\qquad+\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\cdot
\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y)\,dw\,ds\bigg]\\
&=:|x-y|^{\beta_0}\cdot(J_{11}+J_{12}).
\end{align*}
Since \eqref{l3-2-1-} holds true for $\tilde \rho$ as mentioned in Remark \ref{r3-3}(2),
for every $0<\theta<\alpha_1$ and $0<\gamma<({\theta}/{\alpha_2})\wedge ((1-({\theta}/{\alpha_1}))/2)$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{l4-2-3a}
\begin{split}
J_{11}&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,x-y) \int_0^{{t}/{2}}\big(s^{-1-\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_2})}(t-s)^{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}
+s^{-\gamma}(t-s)^{-1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\big)\,ds\\
&\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_0(t,x-y) \bigg(t^{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\int_0^{{t}/{2}}s^{-1-\gamma+({\theta}/{\alpha_2})}\,ds+
t^{-1-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}\int_0^{{t}/{2}} s^{-\gamma}\,ds\bigg)\\
& \preceq  \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).
\end{split}
\end{equation}
On the other hand, note that for every $0<s<{t}/{2}$, $$\tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t-s,x-y)\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).$$
Then, it holds that
\begin{align*}
J_{12}&\preceq  \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y)\cdot
\int_0^{{t}/{2}}\int_{\mathds R^d}\tilde \rho^{x,\theta}_{-\gamma}(s,w)\,dw\,ds\preceq \tilde \rho^{x,0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y),
\end{align*} where \eqref{l3-1-1-00} was used in the last inequality.
Hence, we find that for every $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y \in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation*}
J_1 \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).
\end{equation*}

By estimates for
 the terms
$$\big|\big( {\mathcal L}^x- {\mathcal L}^y\big)p^y(t-s,x-y-w)\big|$$ and $$\big|
\delta_{p^x}(s,w;z)-\delta_{p^x}(s,x-y;z)\big|,$$ we can deal with the singularity
as $s$ near $t$ by the same arguments above and obtain that for all $t\in (0,1]$ and $x,y\in \mathds R^d$ with $|x-y|\leqslant R_1$,
\begin{equation*}
J_2 \preceq \tilde \rho^{x,\beta_0}_{-2\gamma-({\theta}/{\alpha_1})}(t,x-y).
\end{equation*}


Combining both of the estimates for $J_1$ and $J_2$, we finally obtain that \eqref{l4-2-1} holds true.

obtain that for every $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$, there exist a constant
$C(\varepsilon)>0$ and a measurable function $\eta:\mathds R^d \to  \mathds R_+$ such that
$\int_{\mathds R^d}\eta(y)\,dy<\infty$,

\begin{equation*}
\sup_{t \in (\varepsilon,1)}\Big|\frac{\partial p(t,x,y)}{\partial t}\Big|\leqslant C(\varepsilon)\eta(x-y)
\end{equation*} and
\begin{equation*}\begin{split}
&\sup_{t \in (\varepsilon,1),\sigma>0}\bigg|\int_{\{|z|>\sigma\}}\big(p(t,x+z,y)+p(t,x-z,y)-2p(t,x,y)\big)
\frac{\kappa(x,z)}{|z|^{d+\alpha(x)}}\,dz\bigg|\leqslant C(\varepsilon)\eta(x-y).\end{split}

\begin{align*}

u_f(t,x)=\tilde u_f(t,x)=f(x)+\int_0^t u_{{\mathcal L} f}(s,x)\,ds.
\end{equation*}
According to \eqref{t1-1-3}, we arrive at \eqref{t1-1-5b} immediately.
By the standard approximation procedure, we know that \eqref{t1-1-5a} and
\eqref{t1-1-5b} still hold for every $f \in C_{b,u}^2(\mathds R^d)$.

\smallskip

(v) Let $u(t,x)=:\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)\,dy$. Then, according to \eqref{t1-1-2} and \eqref{t1-1-3}, we know that
$u$ satisfies the following equation
\begin{equation}\label{t1-1-11}
\begin{cases}
\frac{\partial u(t,x)}{\partial t}= {\mathcal L} u(t,x),\\
\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}\big|u(t,x)-1\big|=0.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
At the same time, $v(t,x)\equiv 1$ satisfies the equation \eqref{t1-1-11} above. Note that \eqref{t4-3-2} and the time continuity condition hold for both
$u(t,x)$ and $v(t,x)$. Then, using the same argument as in (iv)  and applying Theorem \ref{t4-3}, we obtain
\begin{equation*}
\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,y)\,dy=u(t,x)=1,\quad (t,x)\in (0,1]\times \mathds R^d,
\end{equation*}
which is \eqref{t1-1-6}.

For every fixed $s \in (0,1)$ and $y \in \mathds R^d$, we define $$u_{s,y}(t,x):=\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,z)p(s,z,y)\,dz.$$
 Again by \eqref{t1-1-2} and \eqref{t1-1-3}, the following equation holds for $u_{s,y}$:
\begin{equation}\label{t1-1-12}
\begin{cases}
\frac{\partial u_{s,y}(t,x)}{\partial t}= {\mathcal L} u_{s,y}(t,x),\\
\lim_{t \downarrow 0}\sup_{x \in \mathds R^d}|u_{s,y}(t,x)-p(s,x,y)|=0.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
On the other hand, it is easy to verify that $v_{s,y}(t,x):=p(t+s,x,y)$ satisfies
\eqref{t1-1-12}, and \eqref{t4-3-2} and the time continuity condition hold for both
$u_{s,y}(t,x)$ and $v_{s,y}(t,x)$.  Following the procedure above and applying Theorem \ref{t4-3}, we arrive at
$$\int_{\mathds R^d}p(t,x,z)p(s,z,y)\,dz=u_{s,y}(t,x)=v_{s,y}(t,x)=p(t+s,x,y),$$
which is \eqref{t1-1-5}.

\smallskip

(vi)
Suppose that $\widehat p(t,x,y)$ is another
jointly continuous function  on $(0, 1]\times \mathds R^d\times \mathds R^d$
that is bounded for each $t>0$ and
 satisfies  \eqref{t1-1-7} and \eqref{t1-1-2a}-\eqref{t1-1-3}.
For every $f \in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$, let

\begin{equation*}
\int_{\mathds R^d} p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy=\int_{\mathds R^d} \widehat p(t,x,y)f(y)\,dy.
\end{equation*}
Consequently, $p(t,x,y)=\widehat p(t,x,y)$ for a.e.\ $y \in \mathds R^d$ and hence for every $y\in \mathds R^d$.

$f \in C_{b,u}(\mathds R^d)$. Therefore, following the arguments in steps (i)-(vi), we can verify that \eqref{t1-1-5}-\eqref{t1-1-5b} hold in such case.

In Theorem \ref{t1-1} we assume that $\kappa(x,z)$ is independent of $z$.
According to its proof, the reason why we need such condition is only due to that this implies the
gradient estimate \eqref{p1-1-1}. Thus, for the upper bound estimates for $|\nabla p^y(t,x)|$
and  $|\nabla^2 p^y(t,x)|$, the time singularity factor $t^{-{1/\alpha(y)}}$ will not appear when $|x|$ is large and $t$ is small. This point is

Now, we turn to these two assumptions in Remark \ref{rrr-000}(1). According to \cite[Theorem 1.5]{KR} and  \cite[Corollary 7 and Theorem 21]{BGR}, the following gradient estimate \begin{equation*}

\end{equation*} holds for all $t \in (0,1]$ and $x\in\mathds R^d$ with $|x|$ is large,
which also ensures that
the required estimates \eqref{l2-1-2} and \eqref{p3-1-1a-1} hold true.
